text:
mike_infra: kicking off a canary terraform apply for release/2026.03.20 — primary scope: IAM role tweak, LB target group tag, and rate-limit null resource. change window 02:00-03:00 UTC. deploy-bot will run in canary pool (az-1) in ~5m. ping if you see any red flags.

amy_release: on it. confirm commit: https://git.redwood/infra/commit/8f3d2a — are we pinning provider versions for this run? also add -parallelism suggestion if needed.

deploy-bot: plan finished in canary pool: 3 to change (aws_iam_role.app, aws_lb_target_group.app_tg, null_resource/rlimit). plan output: 
```
~ aws_iam_role.app
~ aws_lb_target_group.app_tg
~ null_resource.ratelimit
```
Applying in 4m unless blocked :eyes:

kevin_sre: quick rollbacks: if iam role apply fails (attach/detach race) we should revert to tfstate snapshot tagged release/2026-03-18 and reapply only networking. runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/iam-apply-rollback

lina_eng: saw a spike of 502s last time with parallelism=10. recommend `-parallelism=4` and add provider pin in the module root: `provider "aws" { version = ">= 4.30.0, < 4.35.0" }` so kernel/provider drift doesn't hit us mid-apply. small change in modules/iam/main.tf, nothing cross-account.

infra-oncall: i'm on watch for the window. i'll tail the control plane logs and can trigger the manual fallback if errors >5% in 5m. pager is armed.

amy_release: agree to -parallelism=4 + provider pin. also set deploy-bot flag `--rollback-on-failure=true` so it auto-reverts the canary and unblocks rollout.

mike_infra: flags set on deploy-bot job: `--parallelism=4 --rollback-on-failure=true --canary-az=az-1`. starting apply now. abort criteria: >5% error rate for 5m OR any IAM attach errors. will post artifacts (plan id, state snapshot) once done.

deploy-bot: apply started (job 4987654321-canary). streaming logs: https://deploy.redwood/jobs/4987654321-canary/logs

kevin_sre: noted. if abort happens, i'll execute the rollback playbook and coordinate with release to delay full rollout. ping me in thread with `@kevin_sre` to escalate.

mike_infra: thanks all — will update in thread with final status. :thumbsup:
